title: Cross-Stack Telemetry Consumer Contract and Onboarding Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary

Purpose: This playbook defines a lightweight, enforceable consumer contract for telemetry (logs, metrics, traces, events) across Redwood services, plus an onboarding checklist and automated checks to reduce cost, improve reliability, and ensure predictable downstream processing.

Scope: Applies to all services within the Redwood platform that emit observability data into the central telemetry pipeline (OTLP/Collector -> Kafka -> downstream buckets). This does NOT replace per-team SLOs or data-retention approvals; it is a compatibility and cost-safeguard layer.

Intended audience
- Platform engineers operating the telemetry pipeline
- Service owners integrating telemetry
- Dashboard and alert authors
- SREs and cost-ops reviewers

Definitions
- Producer: any service emitting telemetry (metric, span, log, or event) into the central pipeline.
- Consumer: downstream system or dashboard reading telemetry (alerting, billing, ML features).
- Consumer Contract: set of guarantees a Producer must meet so Consumers can rely on the data schema, sampling, retention, and cost tags.
- Cost Tag: a small set of labels (tenant, product, cost-center) that are required for tokenized billing and quota tracking.

Principles
1) Predictability: Consumers must declare schema (name, type, cardinality) via the registry before production traffic.
2) Minimality: Producers should emit only fields required by consumers; free-form payloads are discouraged.
3) Observability-as-contract: The telemetry stream is a public API; changes must follow a rollout and deprecation process.
4) Cost-awareness: High-cardinality dimensions must be gated behind approval and cost tags.

Contract Specification (checklist for Producers)
1) Registry entry: create a Telemetry Registry item with the following fields:
   - logical_name (string)
   - owner (team/alias)
   - signal_type (metric|span|log|event)
   - schema_sample (example JSON payload)
   - expected_cardinality (low|medium|high)
   - retention_tier (hot:30d|warm:90d|cold:365d|ephemeral:7d)
   - cost_tags (comma-separated: tenant, product, cost-center)
   - rollout_plan_url (link to PR/Runbook)

2) Schema rules:
   - Metrics: use stable metric names (snake_case), attach unit and monotonicity in the registry. No labels with >1k unique values by default.
   - Spans: include service.name and trace_id; avoid embedding large payloads in attributes.
   - Logs: structured JSON preferred; include log.level and event_type when available.
   - Events: attach event_version and canonical_id.

3) Sampling & Pre-aggregation:
   - Default sampling policy: 1/1000 for debug traces, 1/100 for high-frequency spans unless flagged as critical.
   - High-fidelity paths: for requests marked critical (error, billing, admin workflow) set sampling=1. A field `sampling_reason` must be present if sampling != default.
   - Producers should emit pre-aggregated counters where possible for high-cardinality metrics.

4) Cost & Retention
   - Cost tags mandatory for any telemetry charged to product lines. Missing cost tags will route data to quarantine and generate an automated ticket to the owner.
   - Retention tiers set in registry; any upgrade to warm/cold requires approval from cost-ops.

Automated Onboarding Steps (Runbook)
1) Pre-flight (developer)
   - Create Registry entry (see Contract Specification).
   - Add unit tests that validate emitted metric names and required tags using the telemetry-test-harness.
   - Add a small synthetic workload test in staging to exercise sample rate changes.

2) CI Gate (automation)
   - CI job runs `telemetry-lint` which checks schema, cardinality estimations (sample event set), and required cost tags.
   - CI triggers `telemetry-contract-check` that validates the registry entry exists and matches code-level schema.
   - Failure in CI blocks merge until remediation.

3) Staging Validation (operator)
   - Deploy to staging with debug telemetry level enabled for 1 hour.
   - Run the `telemetry-consumer-smoke` suite that exercises three representative consumers (alerting, billing, dashboard).
   - Check cost-estimate dashboard: projected daily ingestion and cost impact.

4) Production Rollout
   - Canary: route 1% of production traffic for 2 hours; validate SLOs and ingestion metrics.
   - Promote: 10% for 6 hours, then 100% when no regressions found. Document rollback criteria in the rollout_plan_url.

Consumer Contract Enforcement (platform tasks)
- Telemetry Collector validates cost_tags presence and rejects (with backpressure) any event missing them when the producer is configured as requiring cost tags.
- Registry exposes a webhook subscription for consumer teams to receive change notifications (schema changes, retention changes).
- Nightly job computes cardinality growth and flags producers with >20% week-over-week growth to cost-ops and the owner.

Example: Metric Registry Entry (as text)
| Field | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| logical_name | api.request.latency_ms | histogram; bucket boundaries defined in registry |
| owner | payments-svc | pager: payments-oncall |
| signal_type | metric | counters/histograms supported |
| expected_cardinality | low | 3 labels: method, status_code, tenant |
| retention_tier | hot:30d | default |
| cost_tags | tenant,product,cost-center | required |

Checklist for Reviewers (SRE / Cost-Ops)
1) Validate registry entry completeness and whether cardinality is appropriate.
2) Review cost projection and approve retention tier.
3) Verify unit tests and telemetry-lint CI job presence.
4) Confirm rollback criteria are present and reasonable.

Fail-open vs Fail-closed policy
- New producers in dev/staging: fail-open to encourage iteration.
- Production: telemetry ingestion rejects (fail-closed) items missing required cost tags or with unregistered high-cardinality dimensions; the rejection path must create an internal audit event and a JIRA ticket to the owner.

Operational Runbook: Incident Steps (Telemetry Surge / Cost Spike)
1) During a sudden ingestion spike: throttle producers by priority tier using the ingestion-throttle API. Priority tiers: platform-critical > paid-enterprise > paid-standard > free-trial.
2) If throttling does not reduce cost within 30 minutes, enable sampling augment (global 10x sampling for debug traces) and notify owners.
3) For unregistered producers observed in the spike, create an emergency quarantine and notify on #platform-telemetry with tagging info and sample payloads.

Instrumentation & Dashboards to Create
- Telemetry Ingest Rate (msg/sec) by producer logical_name
- Cost Projection Dashboard: 7/30/90-day projected ingestion $ by owner and product
- Cardinality Alert: UoM = distinct(label_values) growth > 20%/week
- Missing Cost Tag Alert: count of rejected events > 0 (severity: P2)

Acceptance Criteria for Onboarding (must be green to mark "onboarded")
- Registry entry exists and is approved.
- CI telemetry-lint passes on the change branch.
- Staging smoke tests exercise at least 3 consumers successfully.
- Cost projection approved by cost-ops.
- Rollout plan and rollback criteria documented.

Escalation & Ownership
- Primary owner: service team listed in registry.
- Secondary: platform-telemetry oncall (rotation) — contact in the registry item.
- If owner does not respond within SLO window (24h for P2, 4h for P1), platform-tier will close the feedback loop and remediate (apply temporary throttles or retention limits).

Backwards compatibility and deprecation procedure
1) Announce change to registry subscribers (webhook & email) with a 14-day window for minor schema additions.
2) For breaking changes (field removal, retention reduction), use a 60-day deprecation window and provide a migration plan.

Appendix: Useful commands & CI snippets
- telemetry-lint (local): `poetry run telemetry-lint --schema path/to/schema.json`
- contract-check (CI): `ci/telemetry-contract-check.sh --registry-url $REGISTRY_URL --service $SERVICE_NAME`
- simulate high-cardinality: `python tools/telemetry_sim.py --rate 5000 --labels 10000`

FAQ
Q: My service needs high-cardinality for analytics.
A: File a cost-ops request; provide a sampling strategy and projected 90-day cost. We will provision a buffered path (warm-only, pre-aggregated) and add explicit alerts.

Q: What if the producer is a third-party connector?
A: Treat as untrusted producer: telemetry passes through an ingress adapter that enforces cost-tags and applies default sampling. Third-party producers must designate an owner within Redwood.

Related pages

- Cost-ops runbook: /confluence/finance-and-legal/billing/telemetry-cost-ops-runbook (internal link).

Owner & Maintenance

- Scheduled automation: nightly cardinality job, weekly digest to owners.
